sovereign_country.strategic_role: 西欧核心消费市场、高客单价品牌合规与本土清关

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: France–United States Tax Convention of 1967, as amended by Protocol of 2006
France–China Agreement on the Reciprocal Protection of Investments of 1984
France–Morocco Agreement on the Promotion and Protection of Investments of 1996

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Articles L. 561-1 to L. 561-50 of the French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier), especially Article L. 561-2-2 (definition of beneficial owner), Article L. 561-45-1 (registration of beneficial owners), and Article L. 561-46 (access and consultation); applied through Décret n° 2020-118 of 12 February 2020 and Décret n° 2018-284 of 18 April 2018; incorporated into the Commercial Code (Code de commerce) via Articles R. 123-220-4 to R. 123-220-7.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation or equivalent extract (extrait K-bis / Certificate of Good Standing) for any corporate shareholder or UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry of the shareholder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille where applicable; otherwise French Consular Legalization in the issuing country

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport or national identity card for each natural-person UBO and proposed manager
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing national authority (e.g., French Préfecture, foreign consulate, or national passport office)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified true copy, notarization, and Apostille or Consular Legalization if issued outside France

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement) dated within the last 3 months
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or credit institution in the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or French Consular Legalization, accompanied by sworn translation into French

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized power of attorney (POA) if the incorporation formalities are executed through an appointed legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary (Notaire) in the country of execution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or French Consular Legalization, with sworn translation if required

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, shareholders, managers, and economic beneficiaries against TRACFIN guidance, the French national sanctions list, EU and UN consolidated sanctions lists, OFAC SDN list, and PEP databases as defined in Article L. 561-10 of the Code monétaire et financier. Enhanced due diligence and systematic verification of source of funds are required for any PEP, high-risk jurisdiction, or sanctioned entity. Negative screening results must be documented and retained for at least 5 years under Articles R. 561-16 to R. 561-18 of the Code monétaire et financier.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Infogreffe (Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés, RCS) via the Centre de Formalités des Entreprises (CFE); associated INPI name-search facilities for preliminary clearance
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All mandatory clauses of the articles of association and the registration application must be in French. The company name may be in a foreign language, but must be expressed in Latin script; non-Latin names must be transliterated into a standard Latin-character equivalent and must be capable of being reproduced in the French RCS records. Sworn translations (traductions assermentées) are required for any foreign-language document.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a final name rejection from the CFE/Registrar, the applicant may file a formal written appeal to the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce within 30 days of notification. The appeal must specify the grounds for contestation and may submit a corrected name copy simultaneously. If the rejection is neither resolved nor overturned, the applicant may seek judicial recourse before the Tribunal Judiciaire under administrative-dispute rules. A fresh name application with the same withholding dossier may be resubmitted without penalty.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for a low-risk micro-SaaS business, provided the French registered office is a real domiciliation address operated by an approved société de domiciliation satisfying Articles L. 123-11-1 and R. 123-140 of the Commercial Code. The address must be able to receive official correspondence and permit physical inspection by tax or registry authorities. The registered office cannot be a mere virtual mailbox for the micro-SaaS industry; a physical receiving facility or managed-access office must be maintained in France.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low risk, estimated at 3–5% annual probability for an unannounced on-site inspection of the registered office by the Greffe or tax authorities; inspection probability remains materially low given the absence of physical inventory and the purely digital service model of the micro-SaaS business.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company name availability search (INPI/Infogreffe database query, including similar-name and trademark pre-search)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff for online registry search; prevailing market rate

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of statutory notice in an approved legal announcements journal (journal d'annonces légales, JAL) for the intended incorporation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market rate for online and physical gazette publication in Île-de-France; approx. 200 EUR

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Filing of incorporation dossier with the Centre de Formalités des Entreprises (CFE) and registration with the RCS (including INPI registration)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Centre de Formalités des Entreprises (CFE) / Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff for RCS registration entries (tarif des greffiers des tribunaux de commerce)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Droit d'enregistrement (registration duty) on the incorporation deed and any capital contributions, paid to the tax authority
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Code général des impôts, Articles 810 and 835; fixed registration duty and 0.5% on paid-in capital contributions (where applicable)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille or consular legalization of foreign UBO and corporate shareholder documents (passports, certificates of good standing, power of attorney)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: French consulate or competent appellate court / Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the issuing country
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Varies by issuing country; average 30–100 USD per document, plus consular handling fees

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified translation into French of foreign-language legal documents submitted with the incorporation dossier
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing per-page translation tariff, approx. 50–80 EUR per page

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office domiciliation service (first year) — managed office address in France for statutory service of process
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for French business address domiciliation in Paris and outer regions; approx. 400–500 EUR per annum

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Book II, Title III, articles L.223-1 to L.223-55 (SARL); articles L.123-1, L.123-9 and R.123-100 et seq. (RCS registration); Décret n° 84-406 of 22 June 1984 (RCS organization)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), maintained by the Greffe du Tribunal de commerce (or Tribunal judiciaire) in the registered-office locality, received through the Guichet unique operated by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Guichet unique creation dossier (formerly Cerfa M0): electronic declaration of incorporation, legible statutes, proof of legal announcement publication, certificat de dépôt des fonds (bank capital deposit certificate), and confidential declaration of beneficial owners (RBE)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No legal minimum capital for a SARL. Capital must be fully subscribed; at least 20% of each cash contribution must be paid upon subscription and deposited in a blocked bank account (compte bloqué) in the company's name, with the balance payable within five years. The bank releases funds upon RCS registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: The subscribers (associates) adopt the statutes of the SARL and irrevocably subscribe the share capital as allocated in Schedule A; each share is paid as provided by law. RESOLVED: The registered office of the company is fixed at [address], Paris, France, for the duration of the corporate purposes; the manager is authorized to relocate administrative offices without amending purpose. RESOLVED: [Name], resident in France, is appointed as sole manager (gérant) for an indefinite term, and the manager is granted full authority to operate the SaaS business and open bank accounts. RESOLVED: The managers and associates ratify all preliminary acts done in the corporate name and direct the gérant to file the RCS registration dossier.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of capital subscription bank account and deposit of paid-up cash contributions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French or EU credit institution supervised by the ACPR/Banque de France
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary blocked account in the name of the SARL en formation. Each associate wires their cash contribution from a personal bank account. Upon receipt and identity verification, request the banker to issue a certificat de dépôt des fonds confirming the total subscribed cash capital is blocked. The certificate must state that the funds are unavailable until production of the RCS registration certificate.
required_dossiers: Valid passports or national identity cards of all associates and proposed managers
Power of attorney if filed through a representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries the transaction, provide updated KYC evidence, corporate drafts, and a clear source-of-funds statement; if the certificate is rejected, correct the discrepancy and re-open a compliant blocked account with the same or another EU bank.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and signature of the statutes (statuts constitutifs)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company founders; notarial law firm optional where contributions include real property or special conditions
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the statutes containing the corporate name, legal form (SARL), registered office, corporate purpose (computer programming and cloud software publication and subscription services), share capital, share distribution, associate voting rights, management rules, and general powers of the gérant. Ensure all shares are subscribed in full and each cash contribution is allocated. Sign the statutes either electronically via an approved electronic signature process or in writing; notarization is not mandatory for a cash-only SARL.
required_dossiers: Civil names, addresses, and birth dates of beneficial owners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a drafting deficiency is identified, issue an amending legal instrument or redraft the faulty articles; all parties must re-execute the corrected version before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the legal constitution announcement (avis de constitution)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A legal announcement newspaper (Journal d'Annonces Légales) approved by the Préfet for the department of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Deliver the required announcement text to the approved legal-announcement newspaper. The notice must contain the corporate form (SARL), exact corporate name, share capital amount, registered office address, corporate purpose, the manager's name and date of incorporation, and the RCS company registry city. Obtain the publisher's attestation d'insertion demonstrating publication; this attestation is mandatory for the RCS filing.
required_dossiers: Executed statutes or specifically the publication text
Identity and address of the legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the publication contains an error, immediately request a corrective insertion and obtain an amended attestation; the original publication remains valid if mistakes are obviously clerical and are corrected before RCS filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and submission of the declaration of beneficial owners (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet unique (INPI), on behalf of the Greffe du tribunal de commerce / RCS; the confidential RBE is registered by the Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the RBE declaration identifying every natural person who, directly or indirectly, owns more than 25% or exercises ultimate control over the SARL, including details of their identity, nationality, exact percentage, and nature of control. The RBE is submitted simultaneously with the incorporation dossier through the Guichet unique; the registry does not receive public access.
required_dossiers: Copy of each beneficial owner's identity document
Details of share transfers and voting rights if any
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry queries the declaration for inconsistencies, file a revised RBE without delay and provide supporting corporate documents to prove the ultimate beneficial ownership chain.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic submission of the complete incorporation dossier to the Guichet unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet unique des formalités d'entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr), operated by INPI, transmitting to the RCS/Greffe
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log into the Guichet unique, create a user account, select the creation of a commercial company, and complete the single electronic dossier. Upload the executed statutes, the legal announcement attestation, the bank certificate of capital deposit, the RBE declaration, proof of registered-office rights, and identity documents of officers. Pay online the registry taxes (taxe de publicité légale and related RCS charges). After validation, the Greffe registers the company and issues the extraits K (registration certificate).
required_dossiers: Proof of entitlement to the registered office (lease, domiciliation contract, or property title)
Identity documents of associates and managers
Power of attorney where a professional filer acts
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Guichet or Greffe issues a query, correct the identified deficiency within the time limit and resubmit electronically; if the application is finally refused, reform the deficient acts or appeal to the President of the Tribunal judiciaire as provided under RCS rules.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Establishment of registered office, corporate books and post-registration formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company officers, local planning office (for occupancy), and social/tax authorities via Guichet unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Effectively occupy the registered office (own property, lease, or licensed domiciliation company), affix the corporate name on the premises and letterbox, open the statutory corporate books (register of decisions), and establish minutes and capital contribution records. Complete automatic tax and social registration notifications and the INSEE SIREN/SIRET allocation as transmitted by the Registry; retain the Kbis extract as proof of legal existence.
required_dossiers: Certificate of occupancy from the owner or domiciliation service
Opening bank certificate for the operational account
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS registration is delayed and creditors rely on the pending formation, rehearse the formation acts; if the registered office is declared unusable, procure a new domiciliation agreement and file a change of branch with the Guichet unique.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - ISIC 6201 software operations do not require an industrial license, ICPE authorization, or manufacturing consent. If a physical office is used, Mairie and Préfecture planning rules apply under the Code de la construction et de l'habitation, but no industrial operating authorization is required.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No operating license required. The activity is free under the French freedom of commerce and industry; the sole official authorization is the RCS registration. The SaaS service may require a data-protection registration with the CNIL under GDPR, which is a compliance formality and not an economic/physical license.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de la Transition écologique - Direction Générale de la Prévention des Risques (DGPR), with DREAL field units and Préfecture if a classified facility threshold were ever exceeded
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - pure cloud software operations do not fall within the ICPE nomenclature or the IOTA (installations, ouvrages, travaux et activités) water/air authorization system; no environmental impact assessment is required for a standard computing office.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater, VOC emissions, or hazardous waste. Office e-waste must be disposed of through registered French EEE recycling schemes under articles R.543-180 et seq. of the Environment Code; heat and electricity use is not subject to industrial discharge ceilings.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: For a standard office not open to the public: fire-safety compliance comprises basic electrical verification, portable fire extinguishers, unimpeded escape routes, smoke detectors where required, and compliance with local building codes. Occupational clearance requires preparation of the Document Unique d'Évaluation des Risques (DUERP), scheduling of workplace medical visits, emergency plan display, and, for leased offices, coordination with building owners on shared means of evacuation.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFIP) - French tax administration; primary portal: impots.gouv.fr; corporate and e-invoicing entities portal: www.paiement.pro / Portail Public de Facturation (PPF); customs jurisdiction: Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-owned French SARL: (1) incorporate via the Guichet Unique (formalites-entreprises.gouv.fr), which transmits the registration to INSEE and automatically issues SIREN and SIRET numbers; (2) upon completion of the registration, the Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE) assigns a French VAT identification number (numero de TVA intracommunautaire) generally without additional application; (3) where no French establishment exists, a foreign supplier of digital services may separately register for French VAT by filing the relevant form at the competent non-resident centre (Service des Impôts des Particuliers, Non-Residents) or elect the OSS (One-Stop Shop) procedure for EU supplies; (4) a company requiring formal proof of its VAT number may request a VAT certificate (extrait au registre des operateurs) from the DGFIP.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. A French SARL carrying on commercial activity is a separate legal taxpayer subject to corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, IS) under article 206 CGI. It is taxable on worldwide profits (subject to tax treaty relief) and is a distinct VAT taxable person (assujetti unique) for French VAT purposes. No check-the-box or partnership classification is available by default, and the SARL is not eligible for the micro-entrepreneur individual regime.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: France has no check-the-box or entity-classification election. Available statutory elections include: (1) under article 239 bis AA CGI, a SARL whose shares are held by natural persons and that does not exceed prescribed size and duration criteria may elect, for a maximum of five years, to be taxed as a partnership (imposition à l'impôt sur le revenu); (2) an election under article 239 bis AB CGI may apply where the SARL exercises only certain specified civil or patrimonial activities; (3) for VAT, an election against the franchise en base may be made to restore full input VAT deduction; (4) ATAD hybrid mismatch rules under article 209 D CGI may require re-characterisation of a French entity where the counterparty jurisdiction applies different classification. This dossier assumes no election is made and the default corporate income tax and standard VAT treatment apply.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT - Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée (TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For foreign (non-established) suppliers of digital services there is no monetary registration threshold: a French VAT obligation arises from the first taxable supply in France (notably B2C electronic services under the customer-location rule). Domestic small businesses benefit from the franchise en base de TVA (exemption without input VAT recovery) up to EUR 85,000 annual turnover for goods and EUR 37,500 for services (including digital services) applicable to the French-established party. For Micro-SaaS consumer subscription sales made through Paddle or Lemon Squeezy acting as merchant of record, the platform is generally the VAT collector and registration nexus is managed by the platform.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France does not operate an immediate real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping system. The domestic B2B e-invoicing mandate is being phased in: structured electronic invoicing (Factur-X, UBL or CII via a registered PDP or the public PPF portal) is mandatory from 1 September 2026 for large and mid-size enterprises and from 1 September 2027 for small and medium enterprises. B2C transaction data and cross-border B2B supplies are subject to e-reporting (données de transaction et de paiement) through API interfaces or the PPF. No continuous certification or fiscal stamp is required; instead, invoice integrity, authenticity and readability requirements under articles 289 and 289 bis CGI apply.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is claimable for the supply of goods physically exported outside the European Union (article 262(1) CGI) and for intra-Community supplies of goods to a taxable person in another Member State holding a valid EU VAT number (article 262 ter CGI), provided the supplier retains evidence of transport and files the recapitulative statement. For the Micro-SaaS digital service scope, B2B subscriptions to business customers established in another EU Member State are zero-rated in France and reverse-charged in the customer's Member State under article 58 CGI (customer-location rule); B2C subscriptions to consumers residing in the EU are subject to French VAT at 20% unless covered by the OSS regime, while B2C supplies to customers outside the EU may be outside French VAT where effective use and enjoyment is shown to occur outside France.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (Document Administratif Unique / export summary declaration) validated by the DGDDI customs system
Transport evidence: signed bill of lading, CMR consignment note, or airway bill proving physical departure from France or the EU
Commercial invoice clearly stating the Incoterms, the French zero-rating legal basis and the absence of VAT
Payment evidence: inward remittance certificate, SWIFT MT103, or platform settlement statement issued by Paddle or Lemon Squeezy showing the collected consideration
For intra-EU supplies only: the customer's valid VAT identification number and the corresponding EC Sales List (recapitulative statement) confirmation
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: France does not impose a statutory foreign-exchange repatriation deadline; however, a 180-day documentation baseline is applied in this dossier as an internal compliance benchmark. The DGFIP may reassess VAT before the expiry of the general limitation period (normally until 31 December of the third year following the year in question, extended to ten years for tax fraud). Where zero-rating is not supported with valid proofs, VAT is clawed back at the standard 20% rate plus late-payment interest at 0.2% per month. Deliberate inaccuracies attract a 40% penalty (manquement délibéré); abusive tax planning (abus de droit) or fraudulent schemes attract an 80% penalty. Persistent export fraud can lead to criminal prosecution under article 1741 CGI with imprisonment of up to seven years and fines of EUR 1,000,000, and the responsible SARL managers may also incur personal civil liability for the company's tax debt.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France, acting within the Eurosystem and subject to applicable European Union monetary, payment-services, sanctions, and capital-movement rules. Prudential and payment-services supervision is principally conducted by the Autorité de contrôle prudentiel et de résolution, while customs and certain statistical controls are administered by the Direction générale des douanes et droits indirects.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France uses the euro and has full current-account and capital-account convertibility within the framework of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union, particularly the free movement of capital rules. A French SARL may generally receive, hold, convert, and remit EUR and foreign currencies through regulated banks or payment institutions without a general exchange-control approval. Dividends, interest, royalties, intercompany service fees, loan repayments, and liquidation proceeds may generally be paid to non-residents, subject to distributable-profit rules, corporate approvals, withholding-tax analysis, transfer-pricing support, beneficial-owner verification, sanctions screening, anti-money-laundering controls, and applicable tax reporting. Banks may delay or reject transactions lacking a clear economic purpose, supporting invoices or agreements, source-of-funds evidence, or satisfactory beneficial-ownership information. Payments involving sanctioned persons, sanctioned territories, restricted goods, dual-use items, or high-risk jurisdictions may require blocking, licensing, enhanced due diligence, or prohibition. French residents generally must report qualifying foreign bank, payment, and digital-asset accounts annually to the French tax administration, subject to statutory exceptions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France has no general statutory requirement to repatriate export proceeds to France, surrender export receipts to the Banque de France, or convert a prescribed percentage of export proceeds into EUR. No general statutory conversion deadline or mandatory conversion ratio applies to software or SaaS export receipts. Receipts may remain in foreign-currency accounts, subject to bank terms, tax-accounting requirements, sanctions controls, and accurate booking of foreign-exchange gains and losses. Export transactions must nevertheless comply with customs, VAT, invoicing, accounting, and statistical requirements. Physical cash and certain negotiable instruments transported into or out of the European Union at or above EUR 10,000 must be declared to customs. Intra-EU trade-statistics and VAT reporting may apply, including Intrastat where applicable thresholds are met. Export documentation, customer contracts, platform settlement reports, invoices, payment records, and evidence of service performance should be retained for audit and tax-defense purposes.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole S.A. and the relevant Crédit Agricole regional bank
Groupe BPCE, including Banque Populaire and Caisse d'Epargne entities

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for payments and collections; Low as a substitute for a French bank account used for capital formation, regulated escrow, or all treasury functions. A licensed European Economic Area electronic-money institution or payment institution may provide payment accounts, IBANs, acquiring, card services, foreign-exchange conversion, and international transfers under its authorization and safeguarding model. It is not a credit institution unless separately licensed and generally does not provide deposit-taking or bank-credit products. Offshore digital EMIs outside the European Economic Area cannot lawfully provide regulated payment or e-money services into France merely through an application interface; they require an applicable French or European passport, local authorization, or a properly authorized service provider. Platform providers such as Paddle and Lemon Squeezy are payment or merchant-of-record channels and should not be treated as the SARL's bank, capital-escrow institution, or unrestricted operating account. Onboarding remains subject to KYC, beneficial-owner identification, source-of-funds checks, sanctions screening, transaction limits, safeguarding restrictions, and possible account termination for high-risk payment flows.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: There is no universal French statutory rule requiring every director or shareholder to appear physically at a bank branch to open a corporate account. Remote onboarding may be permitted where the institution can meet customer-identification, beneficial-owner verification, representative-authority, electronic-signature, and anti-money-laundering obligations. In practice, a bank may require a physical appointment, certified documents, video identification, a notarized or apostilled foreign document, or an interview with the legal representative, especially where the company is newly incorporated, foreign-owned, managed from abroad, lacks French operating history, or has complex payment flows. A capital-formation account normally must be opened before incorporation or capital increase completion, and the bank or notary issues the deposit certificate after verifying the subscriber and source of funds. Directors should not assume that remote opening is available until the selected bank confirms its procedure in writing.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign parent, shareholder, director, or ultimate beneficial owner with an opaque ownership chain, nominee arrangement, trust, or bearer-like control.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current articles of association; Kbis extract or incorporation evidence; complete ownership chart to each natural-person beneficial owner; passports and proof of address; shareholder registers; corporate resolutions; notarized, legalized, or apostilled foreign documents where requested; beneficial-owner declaration; explanation of control rights; and certified translations where required.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of capital, shareholder loan proceeds, or initial operating funds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank statements; audited or management accounts; tax returns; dividend or salary evidence; loan agreement; lender corporate records; board and shareholder approvals; capital contribution schedule; proof of transfer from an account held by the identified contributor; and a written source-of-wealth and source-of-funds memorandum.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High volume of small consumer SaaS receipts, payment-platform settlements, chargebacks, refunds, or payment flows inconsistent with the stated micro-SaaS profile.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Product and pricing description; website and terms of service; customer geography; subscription and refund policy; platform agreements; merchant-of-record structure; processor statements; chargeback and fraud metrics; expected monthly transaction profile; reconciliation methodology; sample invoices; VAT treatment; and a written funds-flow diagram.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of Paddle, Lemon Squeezy, offshore payment providers, virtual IBANs, crypto-related counterparties, or multiple third-party collection accounts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provider authorization and legal-entity details; contractual roles; settlement-account ownership evidence; processor statements; transaction-flow map; customer and beneficiary screening policy; explanation of why each provider is used; confirmation that customer funds are not held in breach of payment-services rules; and reconciliation controls linking gross sales, fees, taxes, refunds, chargebacks, and net settlements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, politically exposed person, adverse media, high-risk country, or unusual cross-border payment exposure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Counterparty identification; screening results; beneficial-owner certifications; geographic risk assessment; contract and invoice; end-use and service description; sanctions representations; export-control analysis where relevant; enhanced due-diligence memorandum; senior-management approval; and evidence that prohibited or restricted counterparties are excluded.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistent business information, dormant-company indicators, virtual office without operational substance, or inability to explain French nexus.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registered-office agreement; lease or service-office documents; director and employee information; business plan; customer and supplier contracts; website evidence; accounting engagement letter; French tax registrations; projected cash-flow statement; operational decision-making description; and explanation of the company's expected activity in France.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Frequent transfers between the SARL, shareholders, directors, related entities, and personal accounts without documented legal basis.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Intercompany agreements; shareholder-loan agreements; expense policies; invoices; transfer-pricing analysis; board approvals; accounting ledger; payment-authority matrix; related-party register; and written prohibition on personal-account use except for documented and reimbursable business expenses.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Request for cash-intensive services, anonymous instruments, unexplained third-party payments, or rapid pass-through of funds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written no-cash policy; expected payment-method schedule; customer and supplier onboarding controls; reconciliation records; transaction-monitoring rules; segregation-of-duties matrix; incident-escalation procedure; and management certification that third-party payments are accepted only under documented commercial and AML controls.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route share capital, capital increases, and shareholder loans from an account held in the name of the identified contributor to the SARL's designated capital or operating account at a regulated French or EEA credit institution or payment institution. For formation or a capital increase, obtain the bank deposit certificate, execute the subscription and corporate resolutions, complete the required corporate filing, and release or reclassify funds only after the legal conditions are satisfied. Use SEPA Credit Transfer for EUR payments within SEPA and SWIFT cross-border transfers for non-SEPA currencies. France does not use a general mandatory FX purpose-code regime; the payment narrative should nevertheless clearly state the legal basis, such as 'share capital contribution', 'shareholder loan under agreement dated [date]', or 'intercompany funding'. Match the remitter, beneficiary, amount, currency, and agreement; avoid unexplained third-party funding; preserve SWIFT or bank confirmation, source-of-funds records, board approvals, loan terms, and accounting entries; and separately assess withholding tax, thin-capitalization, interest limitation, transfer pricing, and beneficial-ownership consequences. A foreign-currency receipt should be converted at the bank's agreed rate or booked under the applicable French accounting policy, with realized and unrealized FX differences reconciled.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant Credit Transfer for eligible EUR supplier and service payments, subject to scheme limits and bank controls. Use SWIFT customer credit transfer, commonly evidenced by an MT103 or its ISO 20022 successor equivalent, for non-SEPA payments or currencies. For material or higher-risk purchases, use a commercial documentary letter of credit, standby letter of credit, documentary collection, or bank guarantee with clearly defined Incoterms, shipping or service documents, inspection requirements, discrepancy rules, sanctions screening, and governing law. For SaaS operations, ordinary bank transfer, card acquiring, direct debit, and regulated payment-platform settlement are generally more proportionate than a commercial LC. Every payment should be supported by a contract, invoice, purchase order or service acceptance evidence, tax treatment, beneficiary verification, and three-way reconciliation where applicable. Do not use customer receipts, merchant-of-record settlements, or third-party accounts to pay unrelated suppliers without a documented contractual basis. Apply EU and French sanctions, export-control, VAT, accounting, and fraud-prevention controls before release.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable EUR/foreign-currency forwards with a regulated bank or authorized investment firm, documented under appropriate treasury terms and supported by a genuine underlying exposure.

Non-deliverable forwards for currencies that are subject to local convertibility restrictions or where physical delivery is unavailable, subject to the counterparty's authorization, local-law restrictions, sanctions controls, valuation terms, collateral requirements, and EMIR or other applicable reporting obligations.

Currency swaps and cross-currency swaps for recurring funding, intercompany loans, or longer-term currency exposure, documented under an ISDA Master Agreement or equivalent bank documentation and approved under the SARL's treasury policy.

Purchased currency options, collars, and other permitted option strategies for forecast or committed exposures, subject to suitability, cost, accounting, collateral, and governance controls. Avoid uncovered speculative positions unless expressly permitted by the board-approved treasury policy and accepted by the bank.

Hedges should be proportionate to documented commercial exposures, with counterparty credit limits, confirmations, independent valuation, maturity and rollover controls, hedge-accounting analysis where elected, EMIR classification and reporting assessment, and board or delegated-authority approval. The SARL should maintain a hedge register identifying exposure, instrument, notional, currency, maturity, counterparty, valuation, collateral, and termination rights.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts (comptes annuels) comprising balance sheet, profit and loss statement, annexes, and management report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Commercial Court Registry) through the Guichet des Formalités des Entreprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholders' approval of accounts required within six months of fiscal year-end; registry filing within one month after approval. For a calendar-year SARL, approval by 30 June and filing by 31 July; judicial extension possible.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Persistent failure to file annual accounts leads to inability to register acts, monetary penalties up to €1,500, and risk of administrative strike-off from the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial ownership confirmation (déclaration de confirmation des bénéficiaires effectifs - RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Submitted simultaneously with the annual accounts filing; any change in beneficial ownership, including via share transfers, must be declared within 30 days of the transfer.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to confirm RBE carries a fine of up to €15,000 for natural persons and €75,000 for legal entities, suspension of registry filings, and potential administrative strike-off for repeated violation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return (liasse fiscale) - Cerfa 2065-IFI with supporting annexes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar-year fiscal year, due on the second business day following 1 May of the following year; for non-calendar year, within three months of fiscal year close. Filing is made electronically on impots.gouv.fr.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a 10% late filing penalty, late payment interest at 0.20% per month, and a possible 40% penalty for intentional omission; no administrative strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Statutory audit (commissaire aux comptes) is mandatory for a SARL when it exceeds two of the following three thresholds at the end of a financial year, confirmed for two consecutive years: total balance sheet greater than €4,000,000; turnover greater than €8,000,000; average workforce greater than 50 employees. Auditor appointment is also mandated if required by the articles, for a controlled or controlling company, or for a consolidated entity.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Annual individual accounts must be prepared under French GAAP in compliance with the Plan Comptable Général (PCG); IFRS applies only for consolidated financial statements required by European Regulation 1606/2002.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Every SARL must confirm its beneficial owners annually together with the annual accounts filing. The confirmation is submitted by the gérant and must identify all natural persons owning more than 25% of share capital/voting rights or controlling the entity. Any share transfer that changes beneficial ownership requires an updated declaration within 30 days; failure to confirm or update can block further registrations and subject the company to sanctions.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Registre des parts sociales et décisions)
Register of Managers (Registre des gérants et feuilles de présence)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 200 - 1,500 USD annually for commercial registered office or domiciliation service
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 8,000 - 25,000 USD if mandatory audit is triggered

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% corporate income tax rate on the first €42,500 of taxable profit for eligible SMEs (annual turnover < €10M, share capital fully paid up and at least 75% held by individuals); research tax credit (CIR) of 30% of eligible R&D costs up to €100M; innovation tax credit (CII) of 20% of eligible design/pre-production costs up to €400k; patent box reduced effective rate of 10% on net patent-licensing income.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (losses may be carried forward indefinitely, but each year’s imputation is capped at €1,000,000 plus 50% of the taxable profit exceeding €1,000,000)
